newsitem.title: USA: Argentine firms ink new Escalante crude term deal.
newsitem.headline: Argentine firms ink new Escalante crude term deal.

text.p: Three Argentine oil producers signed a new term contract for Escalante crude with a U.S. Gulf Coast refiner, trade sources said on Wednesday.
The six-month deal supplies the refiner with 12,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Escalante beginning in April.
The price was set at benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus $3.14 a barrel fob Caleta Cordoba, the sources said.
The new contract supplants a one-year term deal with Brazil's state-owned Petrobras which expires in March.
The Brazilian contract was priced at a discount of $3.21 a barrel, the sources said.
The Argentine producers are Astra, Compania Naviera Perez Companc and Tecpetrol.
Escalante is a low-sulfur crude with an API gravity of 23-24 degrees.
